page: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor. Running on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 virtual central processing units across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware profile includes 384 GB of DDR4 system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 3600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. No graphical processing units are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread capacity. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in multi-core compute tests, including a multi-core stress-ng rating of 81319.36 and a PassMark CPU score of 55443.45. Memory throughput is broad, reaching 214.54 GB/s on large uncached read operations. In-memory data structures perform effectively, evidenced by Redis SET throughput reaching 74.41 million operations per second. However, single-core evaluations show limitations, ranking in the bottom quartile across stress-ng single-core (1380.89) and Geekbench single-core (1147.0) runs.

Cost efficiency is heavily driven by resource density and bundled high-speed storage. Combining 96 vCPUs, 384 GB of RAM, and 3.6 TB of local NVMe SSDs avoids the operational overhead and detached volume fees of secondary storage. However, per-thread pricing efficiency decreases for workloads bound by single-core speed or those requiring hardware acceleration, as demonstrated by poor LLM text-generation performance.

This server type is suitable for high-concurrency enterprise workloads requiring balanced resources and rapid local disk access. Primary use cases include distributed in-memory databases, caching layers, batch ETL processing, large-scale build pipelines, and transactional database clusters requiring high IOPS local caching.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor on the AWS Nitro system. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.1 GHz, paired with 384 GB of DDR4 memory, 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic testing indicates exceptional multi-threaded compute density and memory bandwidth, reaching 74.41 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark cryptographic scores. However, single-threaded execution and sequential LLM text generation rank low due to per-core performance limits. With bundled high-capacity NVMe drives and a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, this instance is efficient for distributed relational databases, memory caching layers, continuous integration clusters, and multi-threaded enterprise application backends.
